title: SQLite for Task Pipeline Persistence
Extract worktree Leaf Package
Cron Scheduling Engine
Provider integration via declarative descriptor registry
context: Non-Claude agents were handled by five hardcoded provider switches; Codex/Gemini were stubbed with unknown cost. We wanted opt-in extensibility for more CLIs, including classifying local Ollama-backed models as $0.
decision: A new `provider` package loads embedded + user YAML descriptors that declare exe names, config dir, session glob, and token/model/cost field-paths. Session dispatch moved OUT of the `parser` package into the registry to break an import cycle. Enable-state is injected via an `EnabledFunc` seam (a DB-backed Settings UI is a follow-up, Plan 2). IDE-embedded providers are deferred to `source: custom:<id>` Go adapters.
consequences: Adding a JSONL-based provider is now a YAML change, no Go code. Non-Claude cost is now real or $0 (local) instead of always unknown. The `parser` package is no longer provider-aware.

title: Anthropic Messages API spawner as out-of-process SDK binary
context: The server had no way to run stage agents against the Anthropic API (only the claude CLI subprocess + OpenAI-compat/Ollama HTTP). The anthropic-sdk-go dependency would bloat server/go.mod and transitively affect all consumers.
decision: A standalone binary under plugins/anthropic-spawner (own go.mod, built GOWORK=off) invoked via the existing custom-exec adapter contract, surfaced as adapter_type 'anthropic'. A new LLMSpawnArgs.Stream flag disambiguates Spawn (false) vs SpawnStream (true). The binary reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from its inherited environment; the server locates it via DASHBOARD_ANTHROPIC_SPAWNER_CMD or PATH lookup of 'anthropic-spawner'.
consequences: anthropic-sdk-go stays out of server/go.mod. Adding the adapter required ~1 struct field (LLMSpawnArgs.Stream), 1 factory case (adapter_factory.go), a path resolver (anthropic_path.go), and the plugin binary. New out-of-process spawners follow the same pattern.

title: Shutdown releases streaming requests after a grace window, not immediately
context: http.Server.Shutdown waits for active non-hijacked connections but never cancels their request contexts. Every SSE handler selects only on r.Context().Done(), so with the SPA connected Shutdown always ran into the full shutdown.timeoutSeconds and returned context deadline exceeded — the desktop shell, the CLI's Ctrl-C path and POST /api/admin/restart all hung for 10s. Pointing BaseContext straight at the run context fixed the hang but cancelled every request the instant shutdown began, tearing in-flight mutations apart: tasks/handler.go passes r.Context() into orchestrator.ProgressTask, leaving a stage_run at running with pid=NULL that no sweep case reaps, plus the same shape in checkpoint/git.go, services/worktree_manager.go and api/agents/tmux.go.
decision: BaseContext returns a context built with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), so nothing but the server cancels it, and a time.AfterFunc cancels it RequestGraceDefault (2s) after shutdown starts. Ordinary in-flight requests finish inside the grace window; the long-lived streams are released after it and Shutdown returns well inside its own deadline. The grace is clamped to shutdownTimeout/2 when the configurable shutdown.timeoutSeconds is set below it. Alternatives rejected: RegisterOnShutdown plus a draining channel observed by each SSE loop, and a middleware applied only to stream routes — both work, but both require every future stream handler or route to opt in, and forgetting silently reintroduces the hang.
consequences: No per-handler opt-in and no route registration to maintain; a new streaming endpoint is covered automatically. Quit costs the grace window (~2s) rather than being instant. Hijacked terminal WebSocket read pumps also unblock on shutdown, which they did not before. Three timeouts now govern the shutdown lifecycle — api.ShutdownTimeout, the shutdown.timeoutSeconds setting, and desktop's drainTimeout backstop — and the ordering constraint between them (grace < shutdown timeout < desktop bound) is enforced only by clampRequestGrace and a comment.

title: Drive agents over ACP from a Go client, keeping the protocol on the spawn side
context: The dashboard reads an agent's intent by scraping a rendered terminal: ~1,275 lines across the pty host, screen emulation and AskUserQuestion parsing. The Agent Client Protocol standardises that channel and ~39 agents implement it, Gemini/Cursor/Copilot/Junie natively, Claude and Codex via adapters. A rewrite to TypeScript was evaluated because the Claude Agent SDK (canUseTool, elicitation) exists only for TS and Python. It was rejected: ACP itself has Go coverage, the TS advantage consists of exactly the features ACP is standardising, and the planned fleet requirement (agents on 1-n of the operator's own servers, own keys) makes a single static binary per node decisive, while a TS agent host would put Node on every server. Kotlin and Rust have an ACP SDK but no Agent SDK, so they gain nothing. provider.Adapter was considered as the integration point and rejected: it reads sessions off disk for IDE-embedded providers, whereas ACP is a process we start and talk to.
decision: Stay Go. Implement the client half of ACP in server/internal/acp and integrate on the spawn side via buildExecCommand, not through provider.Adapter. Depend on github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk replaced onto our fork github.com/lx-wnk/acp-go-sdk, with the replace confined to server/go.mod so the published sdk module is unaffected. Keep any Agent-SDK-dependent capability as an optional, local-only sidecar; fleet nodes run the plain CLI path with no Node. Treat ACP elicitation as out of scope: claude -p does not expose AskUserQuestion, so the existing pty path stays.
consequences: The parser, cost and roster paths need no change, because the ACP adapter writes the ordinary session JSONL with the ACP session id as the filename. Permissions arrive as a structured request instead of a screen scrape, and the gate is fail-closed by construction. In exchange we own a fork of the SDK, whose 87% generated surface makes a protocol bump a generator run plus fixes in ~1,451 handwritten lines; ACP v2 is in alpha and a migration is coming. If Anthropic ships native ACP in the CLI, the agent-side work becomes unnecessary and the client-side work becomes more valuable, so the client stays thin.

title: Remote spawner node: ownership, identity, discovery, filesystem and packaging decided
context: docs/architecture/adr/0013-remote-spawner-nodes.md was accepted with five questions left open in its design spec (docs/archive/specs/2026-08-16-remote-spawner-node-design.md): who owns the pipeline for remote work, where identity comes from, how a node is discovered, what the node's filesystem is expected to contain, and whether the desktop app can double as a node. The spec also implied all five gate phase 1, which ships only a token store, an admin CLI and a config file with no spawning.
decision: D1 the dashboard owns the pipeline, a node never runs its own — forced, not chosen: ADR-0013's Decision text forbids a shared runner-slot pool and its Alternative 3 rejects the control-plane/worker split, so a node-owned pipeline needs an ADR superseding 0013; the PID-less async path (stage_handlers.go:103-112 AsyncRunningTransition{PID: 0}, tolerated by sweeps.go:167-169) is the existing mechanism. D2 identity is node-local with several humans per node, mirroring ent/schema/user.go minus provider_login and storing the credential like api_key.key_hash — not the OAuth plugins, because settings/registry.go:108 caps auth.mode at none|plugin and 'plugin' means a browser redirect through the plugin subprocess runtime, unusable on a headless host. D3 discovery stays a manual URL: api/remotes/handler.go plus RemoteSettings.vue already implement and harden it (SSRF-safe URL check, DNS-rebinding-safe dialer, 15s probe, 50-row cap); the only change is pointing the probe at /v1/health instead of /api/agents (handler.go:89-92), and no discovery code gets written. D4 the node clones repositories itself on demand, rejecting 'the working directory must already exist'. D5 the desktop app never becomes a node — a separate server/cmd/node binary plus a Taskfile target; desktop/main.go stays a local shell. Phasing: only D2, D3 and D5 gate phase 1; D1 and D4 gate phase 2.
consequences: Remote work stops when the laptop sleeps, which is the accepted price of keeping orchestrator state undistributed. Two spec errors were corrected: adapter_config.token_ref needs a recoverable outbound secret, but remote_registration.bearer_key stores a SHA-256 hash whose schema comment (ent/schema/remote_registration.go:20-21) says it is 'not usable as an outbound Authorization header', so phase 1 must store the node token encrypted-but-recoverable via secretbox (AES-256-GCM, LoadOrGenerateMasterKey) — not envsec, which is a 16-line deny-list of four env-var names with no crypto. D4 is net-new work with no existing code: git credentials in the phase-1 secret store, a repo cache with a disk budget, and a per-user rule for which repositories a user may clone; project.setup_command (serverapp/di_pipeline.go:38-72) is the natural post-clone hook. D1 plus D4 also invalidate the local worktree path for remote stages: pipeline/worktree.go:23 runs `git worktree add` on the dashboard filesystem, progress_guards.go:73-82 persists task.WorktreePath and stage_handlers.go:77-80 passes it as cwd, so phase 2 needs a /v1/worktree verb rather than the local path. D5 fences off config/config.go:142-152, where DASHBOARD_REMOTES_ENABLED=true already lets the dashboard bind non-loopback and would publish the whole API including the terminal WebSocket that api/agents/terminal.go:90 calls equivalent to remote code execution. Open for phase 1: validation.IsBlockedIP (validation/ssrf.go:26-36) also rejects RFC1918 addresses, so a node on the operator's own LAN cannot be registered through the current form.

title: New agents need a working folder, not a Project; Claude's folder trust is answered only by the user
context: New Agent derived cwd only from a Dashboard Project folder (UI) and the spawn policy allowed only Project folder roots (F-SEC-001), so a Project was the price of starting an agent. A dashboard-started agent in an untrusted folder stopped at Claude Code's 'Quick safety check' trust screen before any session file or hook existed, so it was invisible.
decision: Keep the spawn allow-list as the control but feed it from two user-curated lists: Project folders and working folders (setting spawn.workingFolders, JSON array; POST/GET/DELETE /api/agents/working-folders, sensitive dirs refused). Project stays optional and organisational: projectId only adds --add-dir when cwd is inside that project's folders. Detect Claude's trust screen (askq.DetectFolderTrust, TS parity) on the spawn's terminal, report it in spawn status, route it into the canonical attention queue as a blocking folder-trust item, and answer it only via POST /api/agents/spawn/{pid}/folder-trust on an explicit user decision, only while the screen is open for the spawn's own cwd.
consequences: Adding the first working folder (or project folder) turns the policy from blacklist-only into an allow-list, exactly as adding the first project folder already did. The dashboard never writes ~/.claude.json trust and never uses --dangerously-skip-permissions to avoid the question. Trust detection depends on Claude Code's rendered wording; a changed screen fails closed (no item, no answer) rather than guessing. 3M.1: pending trust is derived server-side from the scan (session-less dashboard-started processes whose terminal shows the question) and carried in the agents stream, so it survives reloads, reaches every browser and is rediscovered after a server restart; one answer per question. Spawn boundaries strip only the inherited CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION marker.

title: Agents are named by Claude Code's session title, categorised by stated facts, and Command shows usage, machine and activity from existing sources only
context: Phase 3N (futuristic Command + Agents). Every agent read 'Claude session 3f2a1b9c'; a per-folder random emoji looked like a category but meant nothing; Command had no usage or machine reading; animations had to stay truthful.
decision: Name: pipelineTaskTitle, then Agent.title (Claude Code's custom-title from /rename, else ai-title; both last-wins, read by the incremental whole-file scan, cleaned to 80 runes), then provider + short session id (kept as agentSessionLabel beside a title). Category: utils/agentCategory from stated facts only (task > internal > desktop > terminal > cli), drawn neutral and still by AgentGlyph; useAgentIdentity removed. Motion: a card never moves as a whole; its top edge breathes while working and sweeps while a tool call is open, needs-you rings once on arrival, failure is a still red edge, stale holds everything still; no success flourish (the payload has no success event). Command rail: Claude usage = /api/usage 5h/7d windows (tokens, estimated cost, budget share only when configured, explicitly not plan rate limits) via shared useUsage state App.vue already polls; This machine = shared /api/system poller; Recent activity = audit log. Resource levels are one helper (utils/resourceLevel), normal is neutral never green.
consequences: No new endpoints, streams or polling; Agent gains additive title/titleSource. Titles are Claude-generated summaries of a session and appear on default surfaces as names; the raw last-prompt is never read. The topology stays still and counts unreported lists as unknown, never zero.

title: An agent's explicit name and icon are presentation metadata saved by session id; activity is not identity
context: 3N named agents by Claude Code's session title, which describes what a session is doing, not who the agent is; the category glyph described how it was launched, not what it is for; Command's 'Running now' summed lifetime session costs beside 5h/7d windows.
decision: New Agent takes optional displayName (<=60 runes, cleaned) and category (general|development|web|document|research|runtime|data). They are validated after the spawn policy gate, never change args or allow-listing, and are saved after a successful launch in the ent table agent_profile keyed by the Claude session id the spawn pins (--session-id) or resumes; custom adapters that cannot be pinned report profile 'unsupported'. server/internal/agentprofile.Store loads the table at startup and the merger attaches displayName/category by session id on every scan. Frontend identity: displayName > pipelineTaskTitle > Claude session title > provider session id (agentTitle); agentTopic shows the session title only when it is not the name; agentTechnical 'Claude · <short id>' beside non-handle names; icon = chosen purpose or neutral 'general' (utils/agentPurpose); launch kind (utils/agentCategory) is a tooltip. Usage: running sessions shown as 'Active sessions · lifetime' outside the window grid with a note; source says API-equivalent estimate, not an Anthropic bill or plan limits.
consequences: No new endpoint or polling; one additive table and two additive Agent fields. Historical sessions are not migrated and keep the title fallback. There is no rename/edit or delete of a profile yet; rows for ended sessions remain (tiny, presentation only).

title: Delete removes an agent from the dashboard, never its work; projectless workspaces are created, allowed one by one, and still trusted by the user
context: Phase 3N.2 asked for Delete Agent, a projectless agents root with automatic workspace creation, a rich three-column Agents grid, a centred agent workspace and closer command-center visuals, without fake data or weakened security.
decision: Stop/Delete act only on a PID in the merger's latest scan (AgentByPID); internal and remote agents refused; running agents are deleted only with ?stop=true (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5s); delete = ForgetAgent (finished card + suppression against an in-flight scan) + discovery files + agent_profile row; never the folder, repository, Git, Project or transcript. Projectless root is setting agents.projectlessRoot (default ~/Documents/AI-Agents), validated (absolute, clean, not / or home, not sensitive, creatable); workspace folder = ASCII-reduced single path element directly under the resolved root, created with Mkdir (no reuse), then exactly that folder is added to working folders; Claude trust unchanged. UI: rich cards with real instruments only (no per-agent CPU/memory, no sparklines, no tags), 1/2/3 container-query columns; AgentModal centred; one shared AgentLifecycleDialog; Command hero/instruments/surfaces; topology rail flow only for workspaces with working agents while live and LocalScope fresh.
consequences: Deleting a workspace folder is deliberately not offered. agent_profile rows are removed on delete; Claude's own trust entries in ~/.claude.json are untouched. Visual convergence stops short of the mockup's invented telemetry (daily usage bars, per-agent CPU/memory, file-level recent activity, tags).

title: Only agents the dashboard launched can be stopped or deleted; everything else is observed
context: Phase 3N.2 let Stop/Delete act on any scanned agent, so Stop killed a Claude session the user had started in Terminal, and deleting a projectless agent left the allowed-folder entry the dashboard had added.
decision: SpawnManager writes a managed_agent row (Claude session id it pinned/resumed + the PID it launched, cwd, and for projectless spawns workspace_created + the exact allowed_folder entry) after launch; a spawn without a session id is owned only via this run's in-memory spawnStore while running. Agent.dashboardOwned = record matches both session and PID. Stop/Delete refuse anything else with 403 {external:true} and never signal; pipeline agents 403 {managedBy:pipeline}. Projectless workspaces are created only inside POST /api/agents/spawn (projectless:true) so provenance is server-side; failed spawns roll back. Owned Delete removes the allowed entry only when the record says the dashboard added it, no other managed record uses that folder (canonical path compare) and it is still listed; ~/.claude.json is never touched. DELETE /api/agents/{pid}/profile removes presentation metadata for any session.
consequences: Agents spawned before the table existed, or whose record failed to save, are observe-only (fail closed). A dashboard session resumed from a terminal is a new PID and therefore external. Other allowed-folder users that are not managed agents (e.g. a terminal Claude in the same folder) do not block removal of the dashboard-added entry; that only affects future dashboard spawns, not running sessions.

title: Legacy and external sessions become dashboard-managed only by an explicit resume as a new dashboard launch
context: Phase 3N.2.2: a dashboard-created agent (Timer) showed Observe only because it predates managed_agents. Discovery files and tokens are shared with `agent-dashboard live`, and there is no spawn audit with a PID, so no reliable provenance exists to migrate it.
decision: No automatic reconciliation. Ownership remains session id + launched PID. GET /api/agents/{pid}/control reports owned/resume availability on demand. POST /api/agents/{pid}/resume-under-dashboard, after confirmation, resumes the conversation with --resume as a new dashboard launch (recorded as owned). A finished session needs nothing else. A running session is offered this only when its parent process is `<server binary> pty-host` and it is live-injectable; the dashboard types /exit, waits up to 20s (504 otherwise) and never signals. The resumed agent runs in the same cwd with the default permission mode and workspace_created=false. Name and icon edits go through PUT /api/agents/{pid}/profile (presentation only, any session).
consequences: Recovering a running dashboard-hosted session interrupts it and drops its original model, system prompt and permission mode. tmux-hosted legacy spawns and sessions whose pty-host binary path changed can only be resumed after they end. A user who manually runs the hidden `pty-host` subcommand could be offered the same confirmed resume; it still never grants ownership of the existing process.

title: Command hero is a fixed semantic network; lifecycle wording derives from existing state; one port link component
context: Phase 3N.2.3: the hero's random polyline read as fake graph data; 'Finished + Observe only + Resume' was confusing for an ended unmanaged session; Runtime Workspaces port pills were not links while Services ports were.
decision: CommandHero draws five fixed nodes (Dashboard, Agents, Runtime, Workspaces, Needs you) whose states come only from props CockpitView already has (agent stream live, working count, attention queue, LocalScope snapshot source); motion is stroke-dashoffset/opacity CSS, paused on visibilitychange, not rendered under prefers-reduced-motion, hidden below xl. lifecyclePresentation(agent) maps dashboardOwned + running + pipelineTaskId to owned/observed/ended-unmanaged/pipeline presentation with no new backend state. LocalServicePort is the single port pill for Runtime surfaces, built on localServiceUrl; process port lists stay plain because they carry no protocol/bind data.
consequences: No new polling or endpoints. The network intentionally shows categories, not per-item telemetry; if it ever needs more meaning, it should gain it from real state, not more nodes.

title: Phase 4 orchestration is a view over task + stage_run, not a new run model
context: Phase 4A asked for runs, stages, roles, handoffs, attention, failure, bounded retries/review loops and recovery. The task pipeline already persists and enforces all of them.
decision: ADR-0014: Run = task, execution = stage_run, role = stage, handoff = structured stage output, attention = awaiting_user/permission requests via Needs you, bounds = max_iterations/maxAutoRetries/maxParallelOrchestrators/plan cap, recovery = DecideRecovery + sweeps. Clients use src/utils/runState.ts (queued/preparing/running/waiting_user/succeeded/failed/cancelled, timeline) derived from persisted fields only; failure categories only where persisted state proves them.
consequences: No duplicate run tables. Gaps: per-stage output schemas for backlog/plan_review/implementation, a persisted failure_category, a Project Manager role above tasks.

title: Project roadmaps are normalized rows with server-assigned provenance and an explicit current phase
context: Phase 4B asked for a Project Intelligence roadmap that never fabricates progress and distinguishes user-defined, dashboard-verified and AI-suggested information.
decision: roadmap_phase and roadmap_item rows (cascade from project), roadmap_proposal holding an immutable validated JSON payload. internal/roadmap scopes every operation by project, keeps at most one is_current phase per project (explicit, never first-incomplete), assigns provenance server-side (user on edit, suggested on proposal accept, verified only for items linked to a same-project pipeline task whose status is read from the task), and reports progress only as completed/non-skipped items. AI proposals are pending until accepted (append or replace) or rejected, imported only from a dashboard-owned agent running in the project's folders, and the analysis agent is spawned with a server-written prompt through the normal spawn policy.
consequences: No percentages without items; no silent AI overwrites; cross-project access is 404. Dependencies are a JSON id list validated to the same project rather than a separate table.

title: Specialist agents are projectless workspaces scaffolded from server templates with rules in CLAUDE.md
context: Phase 4C: a durable Resume Editor agent with a stable role across restarts and Resume under Dashboard, without a Project or Git.
decision: services.ProjectlessTemplate (first: resume-editor) is applied only to the folder a projectless spawn just created (O_EXCL, never over existing files) and rolled back on a failed spawn. The specialist's rules live in the workspace CLAUDE.md, which Claude Code loads on every start and resume, instead of a spawn-time system prompt that resume would drop.
consequences: The role is visible and editable by the user in their folder. New specialists are new template entries, not new agent types.

title: New pipeline tasks default to manual autonomy; task folders pass the spawn policy; failures carry a persisted category
context: Phase 4.1 audit: taskcontrol.IsAllowAll treats spec_gated exactly like full — PermissiveAllowList (Write/Edit/blanket Bash/WebFetch…) plus auto-approval of every permission request, only git push denied — and there is no spec gate. spec_gated was the schema/form default. Task create/update never checked cwd against the spawn policy. Failures were free-text output.error only.
decision: db.DefaultAutonomy and the ent default are manual (existing rows unchanged). UI labels state what each level pre-approves. tasks.Deps.CwdPolicy (services.SpawnPolicy over project folders + spawn.workingFolders) refuses task create/update cwd outside allowed roots or in a sensitive dir (403); SpawnStageAgent refuses a sensitive cwd for any autonomy. stage_run.failure_category (nullable) is set by the producer that knows the failure (pipeline/failure_category.go); output.error keeps the reason; clients never classify text. The implementation stage output is validated (summary, completedWork, changedFiles, validation, risks, blockers, nextAction).
consequences: Allow-all is an explicit user choice. A pre-4.1 task in a now-disallowed folder still runs unless sensitive. Budget and iteration-limit failures stay unclassified. backlog/plan_review outputs remain unvalidated.

title: Roadmap updates are user-triggered and proposal-reviewed until an Architect/PM role exists
context: Phase 4.1.1 acceptance: Project Intelligence can be maintained by hand and updated from AI proposals the user reviews (Add new phases / Replace / Reject). The user accepted the current roadmap implementation as good enough for this stage.
decision: For now roadmap changes happen only through the user: inline edits, or an AI proposal they review. Later, the Architect/Project Manager maintains roadmap state as work progresses, through the intended flow Architect plans → Developer → Reviewer → QA → verified result → Architect proposes/updates the roadmap from that structured evidence. The Architect never declares its own work verified: Verified stays server-assigned from linked pipeline tasks of the same project, and User / Suggested / Verified provenance is kept.
consequences: No autonomous roadmap writes before the Architect/PM phase. That phase must add proposal-from-structured-evidence, not direct writes, and must not bypass the provenance rules.

title: Runtime classifies service authority; it does not control services
context: Runtime lists every listening port on the machine. Stop/Restart needs a resource identity the server can re-verify at the moment of the click. The dashboard proves it owns an AGENT with a managed_agent row (this server launched that process; session id + pid must both match). No equivalent exists for a service: a service's pid is the listening process, an agent's is the CLI, and nothing the dashboard reads links the two (documented in useAgentServices.ts).
decision: Ship classification and protection only. GET /api/system/self reports the server's own pid, bound address and working directory, and each service is classified by equality against it: dashboard-server (pid match), dashboard-ui (serves the page being viewed, or runs in the server's own cwd), agent-workspace (same workspace as an agent the dashboard started - attribution, not ownership), external. The first two are marked protected. No tier is controllable, and `controllable` is a literal false rather than a per-row field.
consequences: Runtime can say what the dashboard knows about each service without implying it can act on it. Classification is deliberately not by port number: 13120 and 5173 are defaults, not identities, and the backend was observed restarting onto a new pid mid-session. Stop/Restart stays blocked until a service carries an ownership record the server can re-verify.

title: The main agent is an explicit designation that grants nothing
context: The agent maintaining Agent Dashboard itself was indistinguishable from any other agent. Inferring it from the working folder would name several agents at once and would make the designation a guess about a path.
decision: One setting, agents.mainSessionId, holding one Claude session id - so there is at most one main agent by construction. The badge additionally requires an agent the dashboard started, because a session id outlives the session it named. Main status grants no permission, no authority over other agents and no exemption from ownership. SUPERSEDED on 2026-09-16 by AD-2026-09-16-permanent-main-agent: the settings key agents.mainSessionId, its validator and its migration were removed, because a role keyed by a transient Claude session id cannot be permanent.
consequences: Because nothing on the server depends on it, the designation can be stored as a setting and read by the client. If it ever gates behaviour, it must move behind server-side enforcement first.

title: NEEDS OWNER DECISION: whether saved agent configuration applies on resume
context: permissionMode and the system prompt are launch-time CLI arguments; claude reads its mode once, at startup. Nothing persists them per agent today (agent_profile is explicitly presentation-only), and ResumeUnderDashboard deliberately hardcodes permissionMode "default". So an agent's posture cannot be edited after creation, and 'applies next session' is the only honest wording available.
decision: Owner decision (2026-09-16): saved configuration MAY apply when an agent is resumed under Dashboard control, but only after the user sees and confirms it. Implemented as dashboard_agent (a durable agent record with its own id, holding display name, icon, instructions, permission mode, cwd, project and role), GET/PUT /api/agents/{pid}/config, and a resume that carries back the values the dialog displayed. The server re-checks them against what is saved and refuses on a mismatch BEFORE ending the running session, so a refusal never leaves the agent stopped. A resume that confirms nothing applies nothing and starts on Claude's default, which keeps 'no confirmation' the non-escalating direction.
consequences: Configuration outlives the process, so a finished agent still has its name, instructions and saved mode. Nothing hot-mutates a running session: claude reads its mode and system prompt once, at startup, and the UI states both the saved and the running value when they differ. Instructions and permission mode are writable only for an agent this dashboard started; a session started elsewhere can still be labelled but never configured.

title: The main agent is a seeded record, and no request can promote an ordinary agent
context: Owner decision: Agent Dashboard Manager is the permanent Main Agent. The previous implementation stored one Claude session id in a setting, which cannot be permanent - the Manager's session is typically started from an editor, is not dashboard-owned, and its id changes whenever a new session begins. A generic 'designate as Main' control also let any agent claim the role, which the owner ruled out.
decision: The main agent is a row in dashboard_agent with the fixed id 'main', seeded at startup against the server's own working folder. There is no route that sets role, so 'exactly one main agent' holds by construction rather than by a rule anyone enforces. The only settable thing is which session is currently running it (POST /api/main-agent/session), offered in the UI only on the main agent's own panel and only for sessions in its folder. The Edit agent dialog has no main-agent control at all.
consequences: Project Intelligence, Portfolio Developer, Resume Editor and any future agent cannot become main. The role survives the Manager's session ending, being resumed, or being started fresh. Main grants nothing: ownership still decides Stop, Delete and terminal attach, so an external session running the main agent keeps every limit it had. Because nothing on the server branches on role, the client may read it straight from the agent payload.
